title: Party-list: legislation is the solution (1)
primary_topics: What and who are qualified to be party-list representatives -- the Ang Bagong Bayani doctrine (June 26, 2001)
The Comelec inconsistent application of the marginalized-and-underrepresented doctrine and Brillantes renewed enforcement
CJ call for Congress to enact clearer party-list legislation as the only real solution
sub_topics: 1987 Constitution: party-list as component of presidential system -- two types of congressmen (district and party-list); organizations elected, not individuals
Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec (June 26, 2001, 9-5): party-lists must factually represent marginalized and underrepresented; nominees must belong to marginalized sectors
Major political parties excluded: they represent the political mainstream
CJ as ponente: those who have less in life should have more in law; party-list as genuine hope and genuine power for the destitute
Comelec inconsistency: Maza v. Arroyo (July 19, 2010) -- upheld Mikey Arroyo as nominee of Ang Galing Pinoy (security guards) despite not being marginalized
Brillantes-led Comelec: re-enforced Ang Bagong Bayani guidelines, disqualified Ang Galing Pinoy and others for 2013; could not dislodge incumbents for lack of jurisdiction
Banat v. Comelec (April 21, 2009, 8-7) affirmed ban on major parties -- slimmest possible margin
Congress despite 20% party-list membership has done nothing to clarify the system
Real solution: definitive clear legislation; reliance on SC and Comelec is at best temporary
signature_phrases: Every election season, the party-list system always becomes a vortex of controversies
only those Filipinos who are marginalized and underrepresented become members of Congress under the party-list system, Filipino style
those who have less in life should have more in law
It gives the great masses of our people genuine hope and genuine power
It is a message to the destitute and the prejudiced, and even to those in the underground, that change is possible
It is an invitation for them to come out of their limbo
the Comelec had been inconsistent, sometimes defiant, in discharging this simple duty
the Constitution left policy determination to Congress, not to the judiciary

stances.claim: The party-list eligibility requirement -- nominees must factually and truly represent the marginalized and underrepresented -- is correctly anchored in the Constitution propoor policy and the Party-List Law, as CJ articulated as ponente in Ang Bagong Bayani: those who have less in life should have more in law.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-citation of own ponencia as the correct doctrine with explicit authorial claim

stances.claim: The Comelec inconsistency -- upholding Mikey Arroyo despite not being marginalized -- was a defiant departure from crystal-clear Ang Bagong Bayani guidelines, but Brillantes renewed enforcement corrects this deviation.

Congressional inaction is the structural root cause of recurring controversies -- despite having 20% party-list membership, Congress has done nothing; reliance on the SC and Comelec is at best temporary since the Constitution left policy determination to Congress.

notable_anecdotes: CJ quoted passage from Ang Bagong Bayani: those who have less in life should have more in law... It gives the great masses of our people genuine hope and genuine power. It is a message to the destitute and the prejudiced, and even to those in the underground, that change is possible. It is an invitation for them to come out of their limbo -- the most idealistic and most-quoted single passage from any CJ-authored decision.
The Mikey Arroyo-Ang Galing Pinoy episode: Comelec upholding a non-marginalized celebrity nominee of a security guards organization -- the clearest illustration of the doctrine being flouted.
Cardinal Tagle closing tribute: he could be the first Filipino Pope! -- a civic-pride exclamation that humanizes a legal column closing.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban takes up the first major party-list question -- who qualifies -- by reviewing Ang Bagong Bayani v. Comelec (June 26, 2001, 9-5), which he wrote as ponente. The decision held that party-lists must factually and truly represent marginalized and underrepresented constituencies, and their nominees must belong to marginalized sectors -- major political parties excluded because they represent the political mainstream. CJ quotes his own decision: 'those who have less in life should have more in law... It gives the great masses of our people genuine hope and genuine power. It is a message to the destitute and the prejudiced, and even to those in the underground, that change is possible.' Despite this crystal-clear language, the Comelec has been 'inconsistent, sometimes defiant' -- illustrated by the 2010 Maza v. Arroyo ruling upholding Mikey Arroyo as Ang Galing Pinoy's nominee despite his not being marginalized. The Brillantes-led Comelec has now re-enforced the guidelines, disqualifying Ang Galing Pinoy for 2013 -- but cannot dislodge incumbents for lack of jurisdiction. The slim 8-7 Banat vote affirming the ban on major parties shows how precarious the doctrine is. The real solution remains congressional legislation: despite Congress having 20% party-list membership, it has done nothing. CJ closes with congratulations to St. Pedro Calungsod, Cardinal Tagle ('he could be the first Filipino Pope!'), and BPI's Montinola.
